t.E1520.agn: In 2018 EFSA saw no need to change the existing acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 25 mg/kg body weight and stated that estimated exposure did not exceed this limit in any age group.
t.E1520.body: Propylene glycol is largely converted in the body into lactic acid and pyruvic acid and enters normal metabolism; part of it is excreted unchanged in urine.
t.E1520.found.2: Bakery products and desserts (as carrier residue)
t.E1520.prod: Can be produced by chemical synthesis from propylene or by heating glycerol with sodium hydroxide.
t.E1520.regx.0: Re-evaluated; the existing ADI (25 mg/kg body weight/day) maintained, exposure does not exceed the ADI.
t.E1520.summary: Propylene glycol. It is a carrier and solvent in flavourings and food colours.
t.E1520.what: A carrier and solvent that allows flavourings, colours and other additives to be dissolved and carried into food.
